solid formulation of a supersaturated self-microemulsion system (S-SuMDDS) for valsartan (a model drug) was successfully developed and the oral bioavailability of S-SuSMDD tablets was 222% of that of a commercially available valsartan tablet (Diovan).
we developed solid formulations of SuSMEDDS for valsartan, and that they showed improved dissolution and oral bioavailabililty compared to a liquefied SuSMEDDS formulation.

solid formulations of supersaturable self-emulsifying drug delivery systems (S-SuMEDDS) can be prepared using solid carriers, and that the resulting S-SuSMDDS formulations have improved drug dissolution and bioavailability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel S-SuMEDDS granules and tablet formulations, which could provide a new approach for improving oral absorption of poorly water-soluble drugs.
the preparation of solid formulations of a supersaturating self-microemulsion drug delivery system for VST with improved dissolution and oral bioactivity.
the formulation and characterization of S-SuSMEdDS granules and tablets of valsartan.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present study has demonstrated the feasibility of developing S-SuSMEMDDS granules and tablets for the treatment of hypertension, which may be a good alternative to the currently marketed VST tablets and capsules.
the S-SuSMESDS formulation of valsartan has the potential to be developed as a solid oral dosage form for the treatment of hypertension.
the present study successfully formulated a solidified SuSMedDS formulation of valsartan that exhibited a high dissolution and bioavailability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we successfully developed solid dosage forms of SuSMEDDS with improved dissolution and oral bioavailablity of VST.
the solid formulation of SuSMEDDS can be successfully developed and it can improve the bioavailability of poorly water soluble drug.
S-SuSMedDS formulations offer great potentials for the development of solid dosage form of a liquefiable formulation such as SuMeds, while improving the oral absorption of poorly soluble drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

S-SuSMESDS granules and tablets are suitable for oral administration of drugs with poor aqueous solubility, and the method used for the development of S-SuSMEMDS can also be applied to other drugs with similar properties.
